In mathematics, the '''Bergman–Weil formula''' is an integral representation for [[holomorphic function]]s of several variables generalizing the [[Cauchy integral formula]].  It was introduced by {{harvtxt|Bergmann|1936}} and {{harvtxt|Weil|1935}}.

==Weil domains==

A Weil domain {{harv|Weil|1935}} is an [[analytic polyhedron]] with a domain ''U'' in '''C'''<sup>''n''</sup> defined by inequalities&nbsp;''f''<sub>''j''</sub>(''z'')&nbsp;<&nbsp;1
for functions ''f''<sub>''j''</sub> that are holomorphic on some neighborhood of the closure of&nbsp;''U'', such that  the faces of the Weil domain (where one of the functions is 1 and the others are less than&nbsp;1)  all have dimension 2''n''&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;1, and the intersections of ''k'' faces  have [[codimension]] at least&nbsp;''k''.
